test_title: PYST 48: SSC GD Constable - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on: 6th November 2021 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A can complete 60% of a work in 6 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. They work together for 3 days. The remaining work is completed by C alone in 12 days. In how many days will C alone complete (1)/({8)} part of the same work?
solution:
**Given:**

A can complete 60% of a work in 6 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. 

They work together for 3 days. 

The remaining work is completed by C alone in 12 days.

Concept used:

The time is taken by A to complete the work = a

The time is taken by B to complete the work = b

The amount of work done = L.C.M of (a and b) = c

Efficiency of A = (c)/(a)

Efficiency of B = (c)/(b)

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

The time is taken by A to complete 60% of the work = 6 days

The time is taken by A to complete 100% of the work = (6)/(60) × 100 = 10 days

The time is taken by B to complete the work = 15 days

The total unit of work = L.C.M of (10 and 15) = 30 units

Efficiency of A = (30)/(10) = 3 units a day

Efficiency of B = (30)/(15) = 2 units a day

Now,

The amount of work done by A in 3 days = 3 × 3 = 9 units

The amount of work done by B in 3 days = 2 × 3 = 6 units

The total amount of work by A and B in 3 days = 9 + 6 = 15 units

The remaining amount of work = 30 - 15 = 15 units

The time is taken by C to complete the remaining work = 12 days

Efficiency of C = (15)/(12) = 1.25 units a day

Again according to the question,

The time is taken by C to complete the (1)/(8) of work = (frac{30)/(8)}{1.25} = 3 days

**Therefore, '3 days' is the required answer.**
